lead.headline: The champ erased 94.56 points and lost anyway
lead.dek: Maye I touch your TDs? was down 94.56 on Sunday afternoon and led by 3:48 p.m. Then Poochinski’s Sunday-night stack took it back, and Breece Hall’s 11.7 watched from the bench.
body: At 1:27 p.m. Sunday, Maye I touch your TDs? trailed Poochinski by 94.56. I’ve covered the defending champion for nine weeks, and I wrote that number down the way you write down the license plate of a car that just hit you. Poochinski’s Dallas stack had done most of the damage: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Javonte Williams and Brandon Aubrey combined for 84.4, including a 44-yard Prescott-to-Lamb touchdown at 11:35 a.m. that was worth 17.16 by itself.

Then the afternoon games started, and the champ remembered who it was. Brock Purdy finished with 26.28. Drake Maye scored 21.26. Christian Watson went for 30.1, and at 3:48 p.m. his 39-yard touchdown put Maye I touch your TDs? in front, 135.7 to 132.3. Poochinski had been parked at 132.3 for more than two hours, a sprinter waiting for the rest of its relay team. By 4:15 p.m. the champ’s lead was 14.84. That is a 109.4-point swing in under three hours, and it is the best thing this franchise has done all year.

It lasted until Sunday night. Poochinski still had Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III in the late game, and at 5:31 p.m. Williams threw a 9-yard touchdown that flipped the lead back, 151.34 to 147.14. Eleven minutes later Williams hit Burden for 56 yards and another touchdown, an 18.84-point swing on one snap. The Chicago stack finished with 37.46. Bucky Irving’s 6-yard touchdown at 8:27 p.m. got the champ within 4.44, and Irving finished with 28.5, but there was nothing left behind him. Final: 181.76 to 175.64. Nobody on either side played Monday.

Now the part that will sting all week. Breece Hall scored 11.7 on the champ’s bench. Zay Flowers, started from Thursday night, scored 5.3. That swap is worth 6.4. The margin was 6.12. The best possible lineup scored 182.04, which beats 181.76. For the second straight week, the champ’s bench had the answer and the lineup didn’t.

175.64 is the third-best score in the league this week, and it’s a loss. Maye I touch your TDs? is 2-7 while ranking fifth in points. Its luck rating is -2.0, the worst in R.A.T.S., and it’s 2-4 in games decided by fewer than 10 points over two seasons. The playoff odds hold at 70%, sixth place holds by 105.82 points over Big Stric Energy, and the schedule hands it Bad things man bad things next. Poochinski, meanwhile, is 7-2, on top of a three-way tie for first, and needs to find a quarterback by Sunday.

games.headline: Big Stric Energy’s Monday miracle never showed
games.dek: Down 56.38 entering Monday with Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson left. They scored 22.66. Bad things man bad things wins by 50.42.
body: Monday morning’s brief called it a rescue mission and gave it 3.4%. Big Stric Energy entered the night trailing 156.56 to 100.18 with Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson to play. Bad things man bad things had James Cook III. Allen finished with 13.86. Jefferson finished with 8.8. Cook finished with 16.7, including a 5-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The helicopters never took off. Final: 173.26 to 122.84.

Big Stric Energy actually led this game from Thursday night to Sunday morning, which is the kind of sentence that only works in fantasy football. The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST scored 11.0 on Thursday night and that was the lead until Bijan Robinson’s 2-yard run at 8:26 a.m. Sunday made it 11.1 to 11.0. It never came back. Jordan Love scored 36.18 and got almost no help: Josh Jacobs 0.5, Tucker Kraft 1.9, Ashton Jeanty 7.0. By 3:10 p.m. Sunday the deficit was 64.58.

Bad things man bad things won with 40.2 points on its own bench, the most in the league, because Matthew Golden scored 32.4, Robinson 26.7 and the Chicago Bears D/ST, a Wednesday pickup, 15.0. Even Big Stric Energy’s best possible lineup, 132.84, loses this game by more than 40.

games.headline: Cherry Blossom makes it five straight, 178.18 to 120.56
games.dek: Puka Nacua scored 35.0, Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns, and AB81 posted its lowest score of the season.
body: AB81 led after Thursday night thanks to 17.0 from kicker Cam Little. It lasted until 7:38 a.m. Sunday, when Tee Higgins caught a 4-yard touchdown and Cherry Blossom went up 26.18 to 22.58. Cherry Blossom never trailed again. Higgins caught another at 8:43 a.m. and finished with 20.2.

The rest was a procession. Puka Nacua scored 35.0, Christian McCaffrey 22.7, Brock Bowers 22.3, Jonah Coleman 18.8. By 3:50 p.m. Sunday the lead was 59.82. Final margin: 57.62, the biggest of the week. That’s five straight wins for a team that started 0-4.

AB81’s 120.56 is its lowest score of the season, and the last three weeks average 122.31. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 12.1. Joe Milton, a Wednesday pickup, started and scored 13.16, which was fine and also irrelevant. AB81 is still 7-2. Next week brings a bye-week problem.

games.headline: Santa Clara’s Finest wins with one quarterback
games.dek: Both teams started a player who never played. Kenneth Walker III scored 36.3, the best game by any starter in the league, and the Finest won by 22.4.
body: This was a busted-lineup duel. Santa Clara’s Finest started Lamar Jackson, now on IR, for 0.0. deeboliciouskins started George Pickens, who didn’t play and is now listed Out, for 0.0. Each team played a man down, and for a Sunday morning it was the best game in the league: eight lead changes, the last at 11:13 a.m. when Jayden Daniels was sacked and fumbled, costing deeboliciouskins 2.0 and handing the lead back for good.

Joe Burrow, the only quarterback the Finest actually fielded, scored 29.54. Kenneth Walker III scored 36.3. Spencer Shrader kicked his way to 16.0, Denzel Boston caught a 60-yard ball and finished with 15.8, and Blake Corum, last week’s controversial pickup, scored 11.8. By 1:05 p.m. Sunday the lead was 24.72.

deeboliciouskins got 31.5 from Ja’Marr Chase and not much else: D’Andre Swift 3.1, Rachaad White 6.9, Jonathan Taylor 9.4. 117.64 is the week’s low score and the fourth straight loss. Final: 140.04 to 117.64.

beats.headline: One point on the bench, one game in hand
body: Poochinski left 1.3 points on its bench in a 6.12-point win. That’s the whole story, really. The champ left 6.4 on its bench and lost. This franchise played the right guys, including both halves of a Chicago stack in the Sunday night game, and got paid for it.

Then it almost gave it all back. A 94.56-point lead at 1:27 p.m. was a 14.84-point deficit by 4:15 p.m. This team doesn’t do anything quietly. 7-2, first place on points, and the best points total in the league at 1,514.48.
Five moves all season. It doesn’t need more. It needs one.
beats.insight: That one move is a quarterback. Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III are both on bye, and Dak Prescott is the only quarterback available, so the projected lineup has an empty QB slot. Bryce Young (19.69 projected) is the best arm on the wire. Claim him first. Poochinski is a 31.3% underdog to Cherry Blossom, but its top-two odds are 81.6%.

beats.headline: Won by 50.42 with 40.2 on the bench
body: This team is very good and very busy, and this week it was both at once. C.J. Stroud scored 36.36 on the bench. Malik Willis, added Wednesday night, scored 4.82 in the lineup. Bryce Young, dropped to make room for Willis, scored 21.34 for nobody. Bad things man bad things still won by 50.42.

That’s because Matthew Golden scored 32.4, Bijan Robinson 26.7, and the Chicago Bears D/ST, added at 8:02 p.m. Wednesday, four minutes after the Young drop, scored 15.0, the best pickup in the league. Twenty-seven moves this season. It’s the price of admission.
7-2, second place by 9.18 points, and a 79.6% chance at a top-two seed.
beats.insight: Start C.J. Stroud. Four quarterbacks are available and the one that scored 36.36 sat. The Bears D/ST is on bye, so the projected lineup has an empty DEF slot; grab a defense before Sunday. James Cook III saw 28.0 opportunities a game over the last two weeks, up from 21.8, and stays an every-week start. Bad things is a 44.1% underdog to Maye I touch your TDs?.

beats.headline: Season-low 120.56, and the Philadelphia problem
body: AB81 was bound to lose one of these eventually. 120.56 is the lowest score of its season, against a team that was scoring 178.18. Nothing worked. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 12.1, Derrick Henry 5.58, Darius Cooper 4.5.

Still 7-2, still in the three-way tie for first, third in the standings and sixth in points. Its luck rating is 2.9 wins, the highest in the league, and its all-play record is 29-34. I’ve said it before: the standings and the scoresheet disagree about this team.
Wednesday’s move was Joe Milton for Carnell Tate at 12:15 p.m. Milton scored 13.16. Now read the insight below.
beats.insight: Seven AB81 players are on bye next week: Joe Milton, Jalen Hurts, Makai Lemon, Dallas Goedert, Darius Cooper, DeVonta Smith and the Philadelphia Eagles D/ST. The projected lineup has five empty slots (QB, WR, DEF and both FLEX) and projects for 98.03. Matthew Stafford is the only quarterback available. Claim a QB (Bryce Young, J.J. McCarthy or Drew Lock), a defense and Carnell Tate, the receiver it just dropped, who projects for 13.81. Santa Clara’s Finest is a 64.5% favorite unless this gets fixed.

beats.headline: Five straight, and still starting the wrong quarterback
body: The hottest team in R.A.T.S. is 5-4. Five straight wins, the last three averaging 187.67, the best in the league by a wide margin. Puka Nacua (35.0) and Tee Higgins (20.2) did the heavy lifting, and the lineup scored 178.18 without breaking a sweat.

And yet. Jared Goff scored 6.3 at quarterback while Bo Nix scored 16.68 and Michael Penix Jr. 14.48 on the bench. Last week it was Nix 19.28 on the bench, Goff 10.04 in the lineup. The bench left 20.38 behind, in a 57.62-point win, so nobody is filing complaints. Yet.
Playoff odds are 100%. The top-two odds are 25%, and this is the team nobody should want in December.
beats.insight: Bo Nix and Jonah Coleman are both on bye, so the quarterback debate takes a week off. Coleman’s usage is the story when he returns: 18.5 opportunities a game the last two weeks, up from 8.0, on a 72% snap share. Cherry Blossom projects for 170.03, the best in the league, and is a 68.7% favorite over Poochinski.

beats.headline: Four straight losses and an empty receiver slot
body: George Pickens started, didn’t play, and the slot finished at 0.0. He’s now listed Out. DJ Moore scored 6.6 on the bench. It didn’t cost the game, because the game was lost by 22.4, but it’s the kind of thing that looks worse every time you see it.

The real problem was everyone else. Ja’Marr Chase scored 31.5. The other ten starters combined for 86.14. 117.64 is the lowest score of the week, the losing streak is at four, and a team that was 4-1 is 4-5.
The odds still like it: 98.1% to make the playoffs. That’s what happens when the bottom of the league is this far down.
beats.insight: Check the injury report before setting anyone. Then lean on Tony Pollard: 27.0 opportunities a game over the last two weeks, up from 16.7, on a 78% snap share. Jonathan Taylor is going the other way, down from 23.7 opportunities to 15.5. D’Andre Swift is on bye. deeboliciouskins is a 55.2% favorite over Big Stric Energy.

beats.headline: Two weeks, two bench losses
body: Week 8: lost by 1.58 with two winning swaps on the bench. Week 9: lost by 6.12 with Breece Hall’s 11.7 on the bench. There’s a pattern here, and it isn’t subtle.

Which is a shame, because the comeback was magnificent. Down 94.56 at 1:27 p.m. Sunday, up 14.84 at 4:15 p.m., on Christian Watson’s 30.1, Brock Purdy’s 26.28 and Drake Maye’s 21.26. Tyler Allgeier, a Wednesday pickup at 1:12 p.m., started and scored 6.6.
2-7, fifth in points, sixth in the standings. The last playoff spot is still its spot. It just keeps paying for it.
beats.insight: Bucky Irving is on bye, and the projected lineup puts Aaron Jones Sr. at running back. Don’t. His opportunities fell from 20.7 a game to 6.5 and his snap share from 65% to 40%. Start Tyler Allgeier, whose usage went the other way (11.1 to 18.0 opportunities, 78% of snaps), and look hard at Breece Hall over Jones. Maye I touch your TDs? is a 55.9% favorite over Bad things man bad things.

beats.headline: Jordan Love carried it. Nobody else did.
body: Jordan Love scored 36.18. The rest of the lineup scored 86.66. That’s the week. Josh Jacobs scored 0.5 and Tucker Kraft 1.9, which is how a Green Bay stack becomes a one-man band.

Then came Monday, and the miracle didn’t. Josh Allen scored 13.86 and Justin Jefferson 8.8. They needed 56.38 plus whatever James Cook III scored, and Cook scored 16.7. The official loss came in at 50.42.
2-7, seventh place, 105.82 points behind the champ for the last playoff spot. Playoff odds fell from 29.1% to 26.5%.
beats.insight: Chase McLaughlin is on bye, so the projected lineup has an empty K slot. Claim a kicker. Saquon Barkley is on bye too, and Ashton Jeanty is fading: 9.5 opportunities a game over the last two weeks, down from 21.4, on a 52% snap share. Treat him as a flex. Big Stric Energy is a 44.8% underdog to deeboliciouskins, 150.37 to 155.8.

beats.headline: Lamar on IR, Burrow alone, and a win
body: For the second straight week, Santa Clara’s Finest started Lamar Jackson and got 0.0. This time he was on IR. There was no other quarterback on the bench to start, because this front office cut one in Week 8 and another in Week 7. It played a two-quarterback league with one quarterback.
And it won. Joe Burrow scored 29.54, Kenneth Walker III 36.3, the best game by any starter in R.A.T.S. this week. 140.04 to 117.64.
2-7 and last, but playoff odds went from 2% to 5.5%. Don’t laugh. Okay, laugh a little.
beats.insight: Fix the quarterback slot. Burrow is the only quarterback available and the projected lineup has an empty QB slot and an empty FLEX. Bryce Young (19.69 projected) and Aaron Rodgers (17.3), whom this team cut in Week 8, are both on the wire. Even shorthanded, the Finest are a 64.5% favorite over AB81, because AB81 has seven players on bye.

smart_move.stat_label: Points left on the bench, in a 6.12-point win
smart_move.headline: Poochinski played the right guys
smart_move.dek: In a game decided by 6.12, Poochinski’s lineup was 1.3 points from perfect. Its opponent’s was 6.4 away.
body: Smart Move isn’t always a waiver claim. Sometimes it’s just setting the lineup correctly in a game where the other guy didn’t. Poochinski scored 181.76. The best lineup it could possibly have set scored 183.06. The only miss was Jadarian Price’s 11.8 on the bench behind Chase Brown’s 10.5.

The decisions that mattered were the ones it kept. It started Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III together in the Sunday night game, and that stack produced 37.46, including the 9-yard touchdown that retook the lead at 5:31 p.m. and the 56-yard touchdown that put the game out of reach.
Across the field, Maye I touch your TDs? had Breece Hall’s 11.7 on the bench and lost by 6.12. Same week, same matchup, same kind of call. One team got it right.

dumb_move.stat_label: Bryce Young, dropped Wednesday at 7:58 p.m.
dumb_move.headline: Cut a 21.34, started a 4.82
dumb_move.dek: Bad things man bad things dropped Bryce Young for Malik Willis, started Willis, and benched C.J. Stroud’s 36.36. It won by 50.42 anyway.
body: At 7:58 p.m. Wednesday, Bad things man bad things dropped Bryce Young and added Malik Willis. Willis went into the starting lineup and scored 4.82. Young, unclaimed, scored 21.34. That’s a 16.52-point gap on one transaction.

It gets better. C.J. Stroud scored 36.36 on the bench. Tyler Shough scored 19.7 on the bench. The two quarterbacks this team started, Kirk Cousins and Willis, scored 20.46. The two it sat scored 56.06. The bench report shows 40.2 points left behind, the most in the league.

Here’s the thing: it didn’t matter. The margin was 50.42. But Bad things man bad things trails Poochinski by 9.18 points for first place, and in a three-way tie at 7-2, those are exactly the points that settle seeding. Win by 50, sure. Just don’t make a habit of donating the tiebreak.

bench_beat.stat_label: Points on the bench in a 6.12-point loss
bench_beat.headline: Breece Hall would have beaten Poochinski
bench_beat.dek: One swap, worth 6.4, in a game lost by 6.12. The champ’s bench decided a game for the second week in a row.
body: Last week this column featured the champ, and it’s back by popular demand. Maye I touch your TDs? lost 181.76 to 175.64. Breece Hall scored 11.7 on its bench. Zay Flowers, in the lineup, scored 5.3. That swap is worth 6.4, and the margin was 6.12.

The Flowers call was made early; he played Thursday night. Hall played Sunday. That’s three days to change your mind, and the change would have produced the best possible lineup, 182.04, which beats Poochinski.
Week 8’s bench report: 19.1 points left, two winning swaps, lost by 1.58. Week 9’s: 6.4 points left, one winning swap, lost by 6.12. Smaller numbers, same result. The champ is 2-7.

swing_plays.headline: Watson completes the 94-point comeback
swing_plays.blurb: Down 94.56 at 1:27 p.m., the champ took the lead on this 39-yard touchdown at 3:48 p.m. It was the most improbable lead of the week, and it lasted 103 minutes.

swing_plays.headline: Caleb Williams takes it back
swing_plays.blurb: Poochinski had sat at 132.3 for more than an hour. One 9-yard touchdown in the Sunday night game flipped the lead back, 151.34 to 147.14, and the champ never led again.

swing_plays.headline: Fifty-six yards, 18.84 points
swing_plays.blurb: Eleven minutes later, Poochinski’s Chicago stack hit again: Williams to Burden for a touchdown. The lead went from 3.52 to 22.36, and the champ spent the rest of the night chasing it.

swing_plays.headline: One Burrow throw, two lead changes
swing_plays.blurb: At 7:38 a.m. Sunday, Burrow hit Tee Higgins from 4 yards. It flipped Cherry Blossom past AB81 for good, and the same touchdown flipped Santa Clara’s Finest past deeboliciouskins too.

swing_plays.headline: A sack, a fumble, the last lead change
swing_plays.blurb: The eighth lead change in Santa Clara’s Finest vs. deeboliciouskins came on a Jayden Daniels fumble that cost deeboliciouskins 2.0. The Finest never trailed again.

features.stat_label: Points from Lamar Jackson, two weeks running
features.headline: Santa Clara’s Finest won with half a backfield
features.dek: Two teams started a player who never played. The one with an IR quarterback won.
body: In a two-quarterback league, Santa Clara’s Finest started Lamar Jackson, now on IR, and got 0.0 for the second straight week. There was no backup to start: the roster carries two quarterbacks, and the other one is Joe Burrow. The Finest cut a quarterback in Week 7 and another in Week 8.
This week the wire was full of answers. Shedeur Sanders scored 22.68 unrostered. Bryce Young, released by Bad things man bad things on Wednesday night, scored 21.34. The Finest made no moves.

Here’s the punchline: it won anyway, 140.04 to 117.64, because deeboliciouskins started George Pickens, who didn’t play, and also got 0.0. A busted lineup against a busted lineup, and the one with Kenneth Walker III’s 36.3 came out ahead.

features.headline: AB81’s Eagles fly away for a week
features.dek: Seven AB81 players share a bye. The projected lineup has five empty slots.
body: AB81 built its roster with a lot of Philadelphia in it: Joe Milton, Jalen Hurts, Makai Lemon, Dallas Goedert, Darius Cooper, DeVonta Smith and the Eagles D/ST. All seven are on bye in Week 10.

As of now that leaves empty slots at QB, WR, DEF and both FLEX spots, and a projected score of 98.03, the lowest in the league by more than 15 points. Matthew Stafford is the only quarterback available.

This is the team that made zero moves for seven weeks, then three in three minutes, and won. It will need more than three minutes this time. The opponent is Santa Clara’s Finest, which has its own empty QB slot. Somebody is going to win a game with a waiver claim.

features.headline: Quarterbacks on the wire, and three teams that need one
features.dek: Shedeur Sanders and Bryce Young both topped 21 points without a team. Poochinski, AB81 and Santa Clara’s Finest all project with an empty QB slot.
body: Kayshon Boutte scored 28.5 for nobody, the best unrostered game of the week. Darren Waller scored 23.0 unrostered, and Maye I touch your TDs? has added Waller three separate times, so you know where to look.

But the real action is at quarterback. Sanders 22.68, Young 21.34. In a two-quarterback league that should start a bidding war, and this week it will: Poochinski (Williams on bye), AB81 (Philadelphia on bye) and Santa Clara’s Finest (Jackson on IR) all project with an empty QB slot.
The best arms available by projection: Young 19.69, Aaron Rodgers 17.3, J.J. McCarthy 16.95, Drew Lock 16.58. Three teams, four quarterbacks. Get your claims in early.

busted.headline: Two zeros in one game, and Santa Clara survives
busted.blurb: Santa Clara’s Finest started Lamar Jackson, on IR, for 0.0, and had no quarterback on the bench to replace him. deeboliciouskins started George Pickens, who didn’t play, for 0.0 while DJ Moore scored 6.6 on its bench. They played each other. The Finest won by 22.4, so neither zero decided the game, but deeboliciouskins is now on a four-game losing streak and the Finest have now started Jackson for 0.0 two weeks in a row.

w10-m1.headline: deeboliciouskins tries to end the skid
w10-m1.blurb: deeboliciouskins projects for 155.8 to Big Stric Energy’s 150.37, a 55.2% edge. Big Stric Energy needs a kicker before anything else; deeboliciouskins needs to check Pickens’ status and stop the bleeding at four.

w10-m4.headline: Poochinski without a second quarterback
w10-m4.blurb: Cherry Blossom projects for 170.03 and is a 68.7% favorite. Poochinski is at 149.88 with an empty QB slot, because Caleb Williams is on bye. One waiver claim closes a lot of that gap.

w10-m2.headline: The champ gets Bad things man bad things
w10-m2.blurb: Maye I touch your TDs? is a 55.9% favorite, 158.4 to 152.28, even without Bucky Irving. Bad things man bad things needs a defense and needs to start Stroud. The champ needs to start the right running back.

w10-m3.headline: Two teams, three quarterbacks needed
w10-m3.blurb: Santa Clara’s Finest projects for 113.41 and AB81 for 98.03. Both have empty QB slots. AB81 has five holes thanks to the Philadelphia bye. The Finest are a 64.5% favorite, which tells you how bad the AB81 projection looks right now.

playoff_note: Five weeks left. Poochinski, Bad things man bad things, AB81 and Cherry Blossom are at 100% in the simulations, and deeboliciouskins is at 98.1% despite four straight losses. The top-two race is down to two: Poochinski 81.6%, Bad things man bad things 79.6%, with Cherry Blossom at 25% and AB81 at 11.7%. The last spot is the fight: Maye I touch your TDs? is at 70% (from 70.3%), Big Stric Energy fell from 29.1% to 26.5%, and Santa Clara’s Finest climbed from 2% to 5.5%.

waiver_targets.blurb: Dropped by Bad things man bad things on Wednesday, scored 21.34 unrostered, projects for 19.69. Poochinski, AB81 and Santa Clara’s Finest all have an empty QB slot. First claim on the board.
Projected for 17.3. Santa Clara’s Finest cut him in Week 8 and would now very much like him back.
Projected for 16.95. If Young goes first, this is the next quarterback off the board, and AB81 needs one.
Projected for 16.58. The fourth quarterback for three teams that need one.
AB81 dropped him on Wednesday while he was on bye. Projected for 13.81 on an 81% snap share, and AB81 now has empty WR and FLEX slots. Go get him back.

usage_watch.blurb: 27.0 opportunities a game over two weeks, up from 16.7, on a 78% snap share. deeboliciouskins should start him every week.
From 11.1 to 18.0 opportunities a game, and 78% of snaps. Maye I touch your TDs? should start him with Irving on bye.
From 8.0 to 18.5 opportunities on a 72% snap share. On bye this week, but Cherry Blossom has a real starter when he’s back.
Opportunities down from 20.7 to 6.5 a game, snap share from 65% to 40%. Maye I touch your TDs? projects him as a starter. Bench him.
From 21.4 to 9.5 opportunities a game and 52% of snaps. Big Stric Energy should treat him as a flex, not a foundation.
Down from 23.7 to 15.5 opportunities a game, scoring 8.05 a game over the last two. Still a start for deeboliciouskins, but no longer an anchor.

rankings.blurb: Most points, a near-perfect lineup, and first place on points. Now go find a quarterback.
Won by 50.42 with 40.2 on the bench. Scary, and a little careless.
Five straight wins, 187.67 a game over three weeks. Still starting Goff.
7-2, season-low 120.56, and seven players on bye next week.
Four straight losses, the week’s low score, 98.1% playoff odds. Explain that.
Came back from 94.56 down and lost by 6.12. The bench, again.
Jordan Love 36.18, everybody else asleep. The Monday miracle didn’t come.
Won with one quarterback. Needs two by Sunday.
